message.text: The base ran the review of record after Codex's adversarial review and the first Melian round, so the fix commits for Codex's findings were part of the code the probe-running review of record attacked. This change moves the review of record to the first reviewed head, before any fix is pushed, and keeps no rule that runs it again. AGENTS.md:202 says the review of record runs again "where the rules below say so", but no rule in AGENTS.md (lines 159, 212, 246) or in the brief says when. The decision says "After that head nothing changes", and its "What it costs" list does not name this loss.

evidence.snippet: Run it after Codex's adversarial review and the first Melian round, as AGENTS.md's order says. Post its report in a pull request comment headed `Builder agent: Review of record at <head>`, with the JSON block it returns, unchanged. Fix each finding as any review finding is fixed: a failing test first, then the fix, and name the fix commit in the next report. A finding the builder disputes is answered on the pull request, never dropped.

3. The three reviews follow in this order: Codex's adversarial review, Melian's own round, then the Claude review of record. The builder runs Codex's review itself, and its own Melian rounds through the `melian round` workflow, as Three reviews before ready says. Each fix is its own commit from a builder, followed by another Melian round, until only policy notices and advisories remain.

1. Codex's adversarial review, which the builder runs on its own branch before the first Melian round and after each fix pass, and posts with its findings in the pull request's report. It uses GPT-5.6 Sol at high effort by default. The design lens now runs on that model and effort, so it can replace this review; [the route decision](docs/decisions/2026-10-24-design-lens-on-codex-route.md) records why. Codex's review keeps running until it meets [the shadow retirement rule](docs/decisions/2026-10-06-shadow-retirement-merged-window.md), ten merged pull requests at recall 0.75 or better, and the maintainer retires it.
After the first head, the rules are as before: each fix pass gets a Melian round, and Codex's review and the review of record run again where the rules below say so.

2. A Claude review of record, which the builder starts from [the review-of-record brief](docs/review-of-record.md) in a fresh-context agent. It runs the code and does not only read it. Post its report and JSON in the pull request, so the coordinator can import it against that head's round with `melian compare "#<n>" --round <id> --from file:<path>`.

- Rounds come back clean on a trust surface, and the review of record finds a P1. Cause: a lens reads and searches; it does not try the boundary. The Opus reviews of record found what rounds missed by running probes. On [pull request #112](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/112) a compiled probe read other processes' environments through `sysctl`. On [pull request #116](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/116) a captured first request showed the verifier was never given the severity it was asked to lower. On [pull request #117](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/117) precedence worked by hand through the real loader showed a merge lowering what blocks. A review of record on a trust surface attacks with probes and runs them.
After that head nothing changes. Each fix pass gets a Melian round, and the rules for when Codex's review and the review of record run again stand.

explanation.whatToDo: Say when the review of record runs again after the first head. For example, rerun it on the final head when a fix pass changes code on a trust surface. Or add that rule to Three reviews before ready and the brief. Otherwise, state in the decision's costs that the review of record no longer sees any fix commit, and remove the "run again where the rules below say so" claim for the review of record.
explanation.whyHere: The learning at AGENTS.md:362 records that the review of record's probes find trust-surface P1s that rounds miss. In the base, a fix for a Codex finding on a trust surface still went through that probing reviewer. Now a fix written in answer to any first-head finding is seen only by Melian rounds and Codex reruns, which only read. The rule the change says still stands does not exist.

properties.failureScenario: This sequence is inferred from the process text. A pull request changes the `melian round` workflow's gate, which is a trust surface. On the first green head, Codex reports that the gate accepts a head pushed by a bot. The review of record runs on that same head in parallel, so it never sees a fix. The builder pushes a fix commit that rewrites the pusher check and adds a test. Melian reruns its round on that commit, and Codex reruns too. Both read and search but run no probes, and neither finds that the new check can be bypassed through a branch-creation event. No rule in AGENTS.md or docs/review-of-record.md tells the builder to start the review of record again, so the pull request is marked ready and merges with the bypass. In the base, the review of record ran only after Codex's review and its fixes. It would have probed the rewritten check, the kind of catch AGENTS.md:362 records.
